Ledgers

The expense ledgers every bill and voucher is posted to. Tick the companies that use each one; a ledger ticked for several companies is shared. Only the accountant can add or change ledgers.

To Account

Every submitted bill and voucher comes here first. Check the ledgers and approve it; only then can it go into a checking report. Postpone it to come back later, or send it back with a note.

Ledger Books

Approved bills, proforma and import tax bills, and vouchers, posted to their ledgers. Choose a ledger to see its entries.

Debit & Credit Notes

A debit note takes off what we owe a vendor (goods returned, short supply, a lower rate agreed). A credit note adds to what we owe (an extra charge the vendor bills). Both show in the vendor statement and in what is left to pay.

Statements

One statement per company, as a PDF. Figures use what is saved, so save any changes first.

Bills Checking Report

Bills CR (bill checking report): one vendor, one company, one preparer. Only bills the accountant has approved can go in. It is then printed, and the admin approves it for payment, bill by bill. A vendor's bills can't go into a report until its opening balance for that company is captured.

Waiting for a report

Reports

Payment Entry

Everything the admin approved and not yet paid, by when it falls due: overdue and the next 7 days first, then week by week. Press Full to pay the approved amount, or type another amount and say why. Choose how it was paid and enter its reference (none needed for cash); cash is only for vouchers, under ₹10,000 to one person in a day. The pencil sets a payment against one bill, or records a discount.

Each entry can be changed or undone for 3 days by the person who entered it. After that only the admin can, with a reason.

Payment Ledger

Every payment and discount, newest first, with how it was paid and what it settled: the opening balance (overdue part first), each bill, or an advance left with the vendor. Proforma and import instalments stay with the proforma or import until its tax bill closes it.

Payment Planning

Total to pay
Set so far

Locked plans. Their lines are on Payment Entry until paid. Reversing a plan undoes it completely: every payment recorded against it is removed and all its bills and vouchers go back to planning.

Your opening balances

Before you start, enter the exact cash you are holding for each company today. It is the starting point for your cash advances and vouchers. Once saved, only the admin can change it.

Cash Vouchers

Cash paid on the spot, in full, to people who are not on the vendor list. Each voucher is either settled from your cash advance, or sent through a Vouchers CR for the financier to pay by cash or cheque.

Reports

Data & Archive

How much the app loads each time it opens, and the yearly close that keeps it quick. A close removes a finished year's settled records after you have downloaded them, and carries every balance forward.

Backups

  1. Back up now. One Excel file with every record, downloaded here and saved to your Google Drive.
  2. Backup & Flush (Super Admin). Backs up, then clears every record except companies, locations, users and admins.
  3. Flush & Reset (Super Admin). Backs up, then keeps everything still being worked on (drafts, postponed bills, bills and reports not yet processed, open proformas and imports, vouchers not yet approved or paid, locked plans with something left to pay) and folds everything settled into each vendor's opening balance, with its overdue part, and each person's opening cash.
  4. Restore from backup (Super Admin). Puts the app back exactly as a backup file has it.

What is stored

Close a financial year

  1. Download the year. An Excel file with every bill, voucher, report, payment, cash advance, balance and change, and a PDF of all bills and vouchers.
  2. Close the year. Settled records from that year leave the app; unpaid ones stay. Opening balances are set so every total stays exactly the same.
